newsitem.title: USA: EchoStar close to finding partner - analyst. [CORRECTED 23:18 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EchoStar close to finding partner - analyst. [CORRECTED 23:18 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects spelling of company name in headline and throughout from "Echostar" to "EchoStar".)

EchoStar Communications Corp, a U.S. direct broadcast satellite (DBS) operator, hopes to reach agreement with a large strategic partner in the next several weeks, according to G. Robert Berzins, a Lehman Brothers high-yield analyst who has had discussions with EchoStar officials.
Charles Ergen, chairman and CEO of EchoStar, said "EchoStar is having meaningful discussions with more than one party on a strategic partnership front." He declined further comment.

According to Berzins, EchoStar officials are currently negotiating with a strategic partner that would have the capability to distribute EchoStar products on a nationwide basis. Berzins said the company told him that the partner would also make a "signficant" investment in EchoStar but declined to elaborate.
Berzins said company officials also told him that in exchange for its commitment, the strategic partner would receive certain exclusive rights to market EchoStar products.

Analysts speculated that the most likely strategic partner that would be able to offer nationwide distribution capabilities and financial muscle is Sprint Corp. The two companies publicly disclosed in October that they were having discussions. Sprint declined to comment.

Sprint is the only U.S. long-distrance company that has yet to invest in DBS. AT&T Corp has purchased a 2.5 percent interest in DirecTV, a EchoStar competitor. MCI Communications Corp and News Corp Ltd have formed a joint venture to develop a DBS system known as "ASkyB."
Analysts said, however, that EchoStar is also likely to be negotiating with regional Bell operating companies (RBOCs), who are also seeking to break into the video distribution business.
RBOCs such as Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp are believed to be considering investing in DBS technology after their unfruitful venture with wireless cable.

Market players had expected EchoStar to reach an agreement with a strategic partner by the end of 1996. Referring to the status of the talks, an EchoStar official said, "Large companies take a long time to come to decisions."
Analysts agreed that a strategic partnership announcement may be near.
"There are indications something is brewing," said Jimmy Schaeffler a DBS analyst at Carmel Group, a media research company. "I wouldn't be surprised to see an announcement in the first quarter."

Berzins said an agreement could have positive implications for EchoStar bond investors. "What bond investors would really like to see is some equity to come from a third party source, in combination with a distribution commitment."

EchoStar is considered a credible player in the fast- growing DBS industry by industry analsyts. The company already has two satellites in operation and has reserved slots to launch two more. This gives EchoStar the potential to offer more channels to its customers than any other DBS provider currently.

EchoStar stock jumped to 26-1/2 on January 8 from a 12-month low of 21-1/4 during the week of December 27 on rumors of the negotiations, market sources said. The stock traded as high as 40 in January of 1996. Late in the session, EchoStar was trading at 23-1/64, off 7/64.
EchoStar's zero-coupon bonds jumped one point last week.
